title: Free online form maker, no account: replies only you can read · {name}
description: Turn a list into an online form for sign-ups, guests or orders. Replies are sealed in the visitor’s browser and come back as rows of your list. Free.
h1: Put a form online, and get the replies as rows only you can read.
acts: and get the replies as rows only you can read.
lede: Ask {name} for a list to keep: volunteers, guests, orders. Tick the columns to ask people, and its form goes online at an address you share. Each reply is sealed in the visitor’s browser and comes into your list as a row. The host that holds it until then can’t read it, and neither can we.
cta: Try it with a sample sign-up list
facts: No account, for you or for them
Replies sealed before they are sent
try.ask: Make a collection for the volunteers of our school’s spring fair: their name, their email, their shift (morning, afternoon or evening), whether they bring a cake, and a note. Add a column for their stall and one to tick once I have confirmed them. Then tell me how to put its form online.
pane.ask: A list of the volunteers for our spring fair, with a form for them to sign up.
pane.title: A collection and its form, live in {name}
pane.try: This is a real collection, beside its form as people see it online. Fill the form in and send it: your reply comes into the list as a row. Stall and Confirmed aren’t asked: they stay yours to fill.
pane.asked: Here, your reply came straight in. Online, it is sealed in the visitor’s browser and waits at the host, which can’t read it, until you next open {name}.

exact.title: Sealed before it leaves their browser.
exact.why: Most form tools read every reply on their servers. Here, what people send is locked on their own device, to a key only yours hold.
exact.cards: What a visitor sends is encrypted on their device before it goes, to a key made when your form went online.
A host that can’t read it
The host keeps each reply until your {name} collects it, a month at most. It holds no key to open one.
Replies are opened in your browser, with a secret kept there. A recovery code, given when the form goes online, opens them on another device.
where.title: Where your list lives.
where.why: On your devices. Online, there is only the form, and replies nobody else can open.
where.cards: Your collection is plain files in your browser, encrypted. Nothing we can read reaches us.
To an AI only when you ask
Putting the form online and collecting replies use no AI. Rows go to the AI you chose only when you ask it about them.
The form holds the list’s name and the columns you ticked, nothing else. The other columns, and every row, stay with you.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. Asking for the list needs an AI. Making one by hand, putting its form online and collecting replies need none.
A form asks words, numbers, dates, one choice, boxes to tick, links, emails and phone numbers. No file to attach, no second page, no question that depends on another, no payment.
Online, the form is at a name you pick followed by .hst.ing, for a year from each time you put it online. Rename or add a column, and it must go online again.
Replies come in when you open {name}: nothing tells you of one while it is closed. The host keeps them a month at most, and 500 at a time.
Anyone with the link can reply, and more than once. Visitors don’t sign in, and nothing checks that an email is theirs.
A visitor gets no copy of their reply and can’t change it. To confirm, write to them yourself.
Replies open only with the secret in your browser or its recovery code. Lose both, and nobody can read them.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}, for you or for the people who reply. Asking for the list uses an AI, which may want an account: {free} opens a free one. Making the list by hand needs none.
No. The form is a web page: they open its link on any phone or computer, fill it in and send.
You. Each one is sealed in the visitor’s browser, to a key your {name} holds. The host that keeps it can’t open it, and neither can we.
Into the collection the form was made from: a row for each, every field in its column. They come in when you open {name}.
Yes: take it offline whenever you like. Replies already sent still come in.
Yes. The form is in the language {name} is set to, right to left too, with your own words for each question.
